result: I fixed `ProfileController.update` in `app/Http/Controllers/ProfileController.ts`: it now calls `this.validateBody(ProfileUpdateSchema)` (the existing, previously-unused `ProfileValidator.ts`, which already enforced required/trimmed name ≤120 chars, well-formed lowercased email, and an optional 8+ char password) instead of reading the raw request body, and persists via `User.update()` instead of `User.forceUpdate()` so the model's fillable allowlist (`name`/`email`/`password`) silently rejects any stray fields like `id` or `passwordHash` rather than mass-assigning them. Added `tests/ProfileController.test.ts` covering: malformed email rejected with no DB change, empty name rejected, extraneous fields (`id`, `passwordHash`) ignored while legitimate fields still save, and a valid update trimming/lowercasing correctly. Both `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` pass, and `bunx guren check` shows no new issues.
